completedProposalChoices: createNode remains sole node factory; mutually exclusive ordinary transport and local-redeemer acquisition factory dependencies.
Factory supplies exact shared clock; active sources are node/generation and listener/dial specific and unavailable to an older runtime that ignores the factory.
One-use sealed handoff owns exact channel attachment, distinct from custody transfer, controller adoption and identity admission.
Observation and exact host control remain separate; a narrow redemption capability cannot attach or close channels.
NodeConfig.admissionUse requires explicit finite acquisition/establishment timeouts and pending/work limits; no numeric defaults or deployment capacity claims.
Pending-use, admitted-controller, acquisition-work, provider-work, native cleanup and issuer-retained references have distinct release conditions.
Core owns data/observation contracts; node owns acquisition capabilities and implementation; neutral transport has no new credential/identity dependency.
Same prepared coordinator covers acquisition and identity commits; identity provider must explicitly support redeemed contexts and match exact issuer registration.
scopeQualifications: New acquisition branch is a homogeneous local-redeemer composition, independent of dial/accept and CLI/browser.
A remote credential presenter must not synthesize local redemption or import a remote monotonic deadline.
Client fresh-key-per-dial, explicit issuer refusal/rearm, concrete proof hooks and browser credential carriage remain separate B6/B50 design.
No current public export, runtime implementation, browser portability or hundreds-of-peers support is claimed.

authorReview.authority: Author reasoning and source readback only; not independent technical or axiom verdict.

findings.finding: Treating every outgoing client as a local redeemer would conflate authentication role with acquisition direction.
findings.treatment: Local-verifier scope explicit; client presentation/fresh-key design remains separate, with no fake redemption or cross-process deadline.

findings.finding: Sealing a token, transferring channel custody, adopting a controller and admitting identity are different commits.
findings.treatment: Separate owner table and guarded adoption; delayed promise/callback work remains charged and terminal authority cannot revive.

findings.finding: Callback fault or duplicate offer could be misread as permission to abort a channel already transferred.
findings.treatment: Cleanup applies only to the current custodian; replay and foreign offers never restore authority.

findings.finding: A finish call or logical terminal could prematurely refund an outstanding acquisition.
findings.treatment: Work release requires composition completion plus actual invocation/handoff disposition; provider and native budgets remain independent.

findings.finding: An admission record call cannot prove issuer registration or crypto verification.
findings.treatment: Issuer's serialized prepared installation is explicit; provider matches both redemptionId and exact observer against issuer state.

findings.finding: Optional fields alone permit unsupported legacy composition to discard the requirement.
findings.treatment: Node-issued active source and separate higher-level acquisition methods are mandatory; no simultaneous ordinary-transport fallback.

findings.finding: Public synchronous registration could introduce a second mutation owner or execute callbacks in the identity commit.
findings.treatment: Explicit bounded non-reentrant entry to the same prepared coordinator; normalize before commit and dispatch scheduler/abort effects afterwards.
